text:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - Tenant-scoped quality regression detected for tenant meridian-vpc (Meridian Health). Automated tenant eval harness reports ROUGE drop ~12.2% after quant profile 'qv3_fast' promoted to meridian-ded-4 at 2026-03-25T07:41 UTC. Affected endpoints: clinical-discharge-summary, meds-list. Possible customer-visible factual errors.

joni (oncall-sre): ack. paging @tomas (ml-eng) and @hen (eng-runtime). tagging @anna for customer comms. creating short incident thread here.

metrics-bot: alert: tenant_eval_fail detected -> tenant=meridian-vpc profile=qv3_fast delta_ROUGE=-12.2 hallucination_index=+3.9

tomas (ml-eng): reading the eval: qv3_fast was auto-promoted last night as throughput optimization. Global canaries used generic prompt sets and passed, but meridian's tenant-specific set failed. looks like a distribution mismatch. grabbing logs.

            logs:
            ```
            2026-03-25T07:41:03Z rollout start: profile=qv3_fast commit=5ab2c1
            2026-03-25T07:51:20Z tenant-eval(meridian-vpc): rouge_delta=-12.2
            2026-03-25T07:51:45Z gen_issue: list_reordering + token_truncation
            ```

tomas (ml-eng): quick hypothesis: qv3_fast's aggressive per-channel 4-bit mapping plus head-rescale reduces dynamic range for short enumerative outputs used heavily by Meridian templates. That induces truncation and re-ordering. Also noted: our canary set did not include Meridian's short-list templates (gap in gating).

hen (eng-runtime): mitigation options: 1) reroute tenant traffic to fp16 fallback (no restarts) 2) rollback tenant quant_profile to qv2_stable (requires rolling restart + KV warm) 3) try conservative hotpatch of kernel (risky). Recommend 1 then 2.

joni (oncall-sre): agree route first to reduce customer exposure. hen, can you apply routing and smoke test? tomas prepare rollback cmd. anna craft customer note. keep updates short.

hen (eng-runtime): running emergency route:
```
redwoodctl route set --tenant meridian-vpc --to "redwood/gpt-clinical-fp16:v7" --weight 100 --reason "emergency fallback due to tenant quality regression"
```

hen (eng-runtime): applied. control-plane shows active route -> gpt-clinical-fp16:v7. running 20-sample smoke batch against meridian-ded-4: responses look nominal, KV caches warming.

deploy-bot: job created rb-20260325-6602 (tomas) - tenant rollback queued.

tomas (ml-eng): issuing rollback to qv2_stable:
```
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant meridian-vpc --set quant_profile=qv2_stable --author tomas --message "rollback after regression"
```
deploy-bot: rollback job rb-20260325-6602 started. applying tenant config to meridian-ded-4.

hen (eng-runtime): scheduling rolling restarts on meridian-ded-4: drain node-a -> restart -> warm -> un-drain -> repeat. recommended safe window ~22-30m. will flush KV caches after each restart.

anna (support): initial note to Meridian Health SRE: "We detected a decline in summarization quality for a subset of your workflows after a quant profile update. We've routed traffic to a fallback FP16 model and are rolling back the quant profile on your dedicated pool. Expect quality stabilization in ~30 minutes. No user data was modified. We'll share a redacted postmortem."

meridian-sre (customer): replied: appreciate the quick response. any chance to see samples of before/after?

anna (support): yes, we'll provide redacted sample diffs once mitigation confirmed.

hen (eng-runtime): restarts in progress. node-a drained. node-b draining. no OOMs. small redis miss spike observed during KV flush, returning to baseline quickly.

tomas (ml-eng): running quick evals (50 samples) against fp16 route and post-rollback candidate. results:
```
pre-rollout (qv3_fast): rouge -12.2
post-routing (fp16 fallback): rouge delta -1.6
post-rollback (qv2_stable): rouge delta +0.4 vs baseline (within noise)
hallucination metric back to baseline
```

tomas (ml-eng): full tenant eval (500 samples) kicked off; ETA ~35 minutes.

deploy-bot: rollback job rb-20260325-6602 status=success.

hen (eng-runtime): all nodes restarted and healthy. KV caches warmed.

tomas (ml-eng): full eval complete: metrics within +-1% of baseline. drafting postmortem. preliminary root cause: numeric drift introduced by qv3_fast on short enumerative templates common to Meridian. contributing factor: canary set omitted tenant-specific short-list prompts, so gating failed.

anna (support): sent follow-up to customer with summary + timeline + promise of postmortem. customer prefers to stay on stable profile until we implement gating.

joni (oncall-sre): action items: tomas -> postmortem + add tenant-specific canary for Meridian prompt mix; hen -> add control-plane guard to prevent auto-promote of profiles flagged experimental to dedicated pools and implement preflight abort if any tenant eval delta >5%; anna -> coordinate customer postmortem call. I'll stay on pager for 1 hour. Incident ticket INF-4999 created.

tomas (ml-eng): additional mitigation: disabling auto-quant autopromote for dedicated pools until tenant-eval gating is in place; adding sample-diff gating that requires tenant eval match before rollout can proceed. I'll open PRs and link them to INF-4999.

hen (eng-runtime): ops note: will add a preflight check in control-plane and a flag to mark profiles as "no-auto-promote". also update runbook to include a check that canary sets include tenant short-form prompts for quant rollouts.

joni (oncall-sre): closing the live bridge. mitigation verified. customer impact: transient quality degradation for ~30-40 minutes for summarization flows only, no downtime, no data modification. leaving follow-ups in Jira. thanks all.

(reacts: :rotating_light: on incident-bot initial pager, :white_check_mark: on deploy-bot success, :memo: on tomas postmortem plan)
